title: Object Suffixes on the Verb
description: Recognize pronoun objects attached to verbs.

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.html: A verb may take a pronominal suffix that marks the direct object of the action, not the subject. שְׁמָרוֹ means "he kept him", and שְׁמָרַנִי "he kept me". The suffix's person, gender, and number identify the one acted upon, while the verb's own ending still marks the subject. These suffixes are the same in form as the possessive suffixes on nouns.

blocks.caption: The forms
blocks.html: A pronoun object can be attached to the verb instead of written with אֹת־: שְׁמָרוֹ (he kept him) for שָׁמַר אֹתוֹ. The endings are those of the nouns, sometimes with a connecting vowel: ־נִי (me), ־ךָ / ־ךְ (you, m./f.), ־וֹ or ־הוּ (him), ־הָ (her), ־נוּ (us), ־כֶם (you, pl.), ־ם (them). The suffix pulls the stress forward, so the verb's vowels reduce: שָׁמַר → שְׁמָרַנִי (he kept me). The imperfect often adds ־ֵ־ or ־ֶנּ־ before the suffix: יִשְׁמְרֵנִי (he will keep me), יִשְׁמְרֶנּוּ (he will keep him). Read the verb first, then the suffix.

blocks.caption: Object suffixes
blocks.html: The pronominal suffixes attached to a verb express the direct object, and they are the same suffixes that nouns take for possession. So שְׁמָרוֹ ("he kept him") and בֵּיתוֹ ("his house") share the suffix -ô. Learn the suffix set once and it serves nouns, prepositions, and verbs alike.

blocks.caption: Reading the suffix
blocks.html: To parse a suffixed verb, first name the verb's own stem, conjugation, and subject from its prefix and ending, then name the object from the suffix. The suffix does not change the subject; it adds the one acted upon. Distinguish a subject ending from an object suffix by asking whether the verb already has its subject marked.

blocks.caption: Common confusion
blocks.html: Do not confuse a subject ending with an object suffix. The verb's person ending marks the doer; a following suffix marks the one done to. When a suffix appears on a form that already has its subject, the suffix is the object. Read both, in order, before translating.

blocks.caption: Worked example
blocks.html: Take שְׁמָרוֹ ("he kept him"). The verb's own ending marks the subject "he", and the suffix -ô marks the object "him". Read the subject from the verb and the object from the suffix, in that order, before translating.

blocks.caption: Reading practice
blocks.html: Read and parse. שְׁמָרוֹ — "he kept him" (subject "he", object "him"). שְׁמָרַנִי — "he kept me". Read the subject from the verb's ending and the object from the suffix, in that order.
